hints: Root the tree and consider each subtree after its children have been processed.
The closest selected office in a child subtree is the first one that can conflict with another branch.
When two candidate offices are too close through their parent, discard the shallower one.
analogy: Keep offices toward the leaves: a deeper office is farther from everything outside its branch.
example: For roads 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 3-5 and d=3, offices at 1 and 4 are distance 3 apart, and two is optimal.
algorithm: Root the tree and process nodes in postorder. At node u, tentatively select u and gather it together with the closest selected office returned by each child. Sort these candidates by depth. While the two shallowest have depth[x]+depth[y]-2*depth[u] < d, unselect the shallowest. Return the remaining shallowest candidate to the parent; all deeper selected offices remain selected. Finally print all selected nodes.
correctness: Within each child subtree, only its closest office can create a new conflict through u. If two candidates conflict, any valid solution must remove one; keeping the deeper one is at least as good for conflicts outside the subtree because it is farther from every ancestor and other branch. Applying this exchange at every node yields an optimal valid selection.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
